preamble: All six-letter solutions are flowers and may not be further defined

clue.text: Secondary action by second, 13th or 15th method

parts.note: in the Roman calendar the Ides fell on the 13th of most months, the 15th of March, May, July and October
how something is done is its method

explanation.surface: Someone describes a secondary action carried out by a second method, chosen from the thirteenth or fifteenth option.
explanation.walkthrough: The ordinals look like items in a numbered list; they are the two dates on which the Roman Ides could fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion or subsidiary event beside the main business is a secondary action, like a fairground's extra booth.

clue.text: Cut to a point

parts.note: to sever is to cut through
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: An instruction to trim something down until it is sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble's 'flowers' are things that flow: rivers. The SEVERN is Britain's longest river, running through Wales and England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Severn is a river, a thing that flows, which the preamble's punning flowers stands for.

clue.text: Boy's turn, live

parts.note: Dan is a boy's name; the possessive adds no letter
U as in a U-turn
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: It is a lad's go next, and the game is played for real.
explanation.walkthrough: The DANUBE is the great river of central Europe; 'flowers' in the preamble means rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danube is a European river, a flower in the sense of something that flows.

clue.text: What's in the mouth with a little twist

indicators.note: a small twist shifts one letter of the word for spit to a new place nearby

parts.note: saliva is the fluid in the mouth

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what is found in the mouth, given a slight twist.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the V of the word for spit one place earlier gives SALVIA, a garden plant (sage), one of the true flowers in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvia is the sage genus, grown in gardens for its spikes of blooms, a literal flower here.

clue.text: Economising for a time, head off to the City and get a pile

indicators.note: the first letter is removed from the period word

parts.note: a month is a period of time
EC is the postcode area of the City of London, the financial district
a heap is a pile

explanation.surface: Someone saves money for a while, then heads to the financial district to make a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head off' removes M from MONTH, leaving ONTH. EC is the London postcode for the City, the capital's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things cheaply is the idiom for spending as little as possible, which is economising.

clue.text: Sam Weller's face doesn't appear with a message

indicators.note: the face word's letters are taken away from the phrase that follows

parts.note: the river runs inside these words only by coincidence of the deletion: the face letters are removed from both ends, so this is no hidden-word device
Sam Weller in Dickens's Pickwick Papers says W for V, so 'visage' (face) becomes wisage

explanation.surface: A Dickens character fails to show up in person but sends word instead.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove W, I and then S, A, G, E from WITHAMESSAGE to leave the London river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thames is London's river, a flower in the preamble's sense of something that flows.

clue.text: I can sting referees let loose among the sacred

indicators.note: the scrambled officials go in the middle of the word for sacred

parts.note: holy means sacred

indicators.note: the officials are freed and scattered into a new order

parts.note: refs is short for referees

explanation.surface: A creature boasts it can sting officials set free among holy people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let loose' turns REFS into RSEF, which goes 'among' HOLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A biting insect that torments horses is speaking in the first person, a riddle-style definition.

clue.text: Slimy character with Greek one very comfortable about it

parts.note: mu is one of the letters of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: the word for snug goes around 'it'

parts.note: cosy means snug, very comfortable
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Greek who is very comfortable is described as having a slimy nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek one' looks like a person; it is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Mucosity is the quality of being mucous, slimy in character.

clue.text: Appeal to a feminine element good with these words

parts.note: SOS is a distress signal, an appeal for help
yin is the feminine principle in Chinese philosophy

explanation.surface: A plea to some womanly quality, good and expressed in words.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said when ending a speech, meaning having spoken these words.

clue.text: Natively inclined to readiness for corruption

indicators.note: letters inclined, tipped over, fall into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone born to a place is inclined to be easily corrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: Venality is the readiness to be bribed or corrupted.

clue.text: American reptile first

indicators.note: says the reptile piece comes before the American piece

parts.note: croc is short for crocodile, a reptile

explanation.surface: An American reptile is listed before everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: CROCUS is a spring flower: a true flower among the rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The crocus is a spring-flowering bulb, a literal flower among the rivers.

clue.text: I'm after creatures on minister's territory

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish minister of religion; the possessive adds no letter
Ter. is an abbreviation for territory

explanation.surface: A hunter says they are pursuing animals on a churchman's patch.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbiter is a person who hunts rabbits, someone after creatures, speaking in the first person.

clue.text: Setter's holding tongue

indicators.note: the possessive word holds the language inside it

parts.note: the setter refers to themself; 'setter's' is 'my'
Erse is the Gaelic language

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler is biting their tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: The MERSEY is the river of Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mersey is the river at Liverpool, a flower in the preamble's punning sense.

clue.text: Islander is leader of Abraham Lincoln's administration

indicators.note: administering the letters, managing them, puts them in a fresh order
the leading letter of the first name is taken

parts.note: the surname as written; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: An islander is said to head Lincoln's presidential government.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isles of Scilly lie off Cornwall; their people are Scillonians. 'administration' looks like Lincoln's presidency but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Scilly Isles is an islander from that group.

clue.text: Explorer's dwelling to supply information

parts.note: a shack is a humble dwelling
to let on is to reveal information

explanation.surface: An explorer's hut is used to pass on news.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernest Shackleton led British expeditions to the Antarctic.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Shackleton was a famous Antarctic explorer.

clue.text: Marry woman that's not all there, morphing into destructive creature

indicators.note: the letters change shape into something new
the female word is not all present: its last letters are missing

explanation.surface: A wedding to a woman who is not quite all there turns into something destructive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not all there' cuts WOMAN to WOM; 'morphing into' rearranges MARRY plus WOM.
explanation.definitionFit: The armyworm is a caterpillar that moves in hordes devouring crops, a destructive pest.

clue.text: Queue to give follower support

parts.note: a tail is someone who follows another
to back is to support

explanation.surface: A request that one gives a follower some backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic queue stretching back from an obstruction is a tailback.

clue.text: Sledge made to low standard going on horseback

parts.note: 'bog standard' is a slang phrase for ordinary or low-grade, so bog stands for it
a horse is a nag; read back to front it gives the last three letters

explanation.surface: A sledge has been built cheaply and is ridden on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horseback' is one word doing two things: horse is NAG, and back turns it round, giving GAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A toboggan is a long, light sledge for sliding downhill.

clue.text: Just a boy, captured by a rebel at sea

indicators.note: the young man is held inside the jumbled rebel
the rebel's letters are all at sea, in confusion

parts.note: a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Only a lad, taken prisoner by a mutineer on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' is the adjective meaning fair, not 'only'; 'at sea' and 'captured by' both look like part of a sea story.
explanation.definitionFit: Just means fair and reasonable.

clue.text: She fought to sell books

explanation.surface: A woman who once battled now runs a bookshop.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses name the word, not the river: the warrior women of legend and the online bookseller. The AMAZON is the great river of South America, a 'flower' in the preamble's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazon is South America's greatest river, a flower in the preamble's sense.

clue.text: Trouble had arisen

indicators.note: in a down entry the words rise, read from the bottom up

parts.note: to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Trouble had come up.
explanation.walkthrough: DAHLIA is a garden flower, a true flower here.
explanation.definitionFit: The dahlia is a showy garden bloom, a literal flower among the rivers.

clue.text: Boy out of hospital

indicators.note: the boy is let out, so the hospital letter leaves him

parts.note: Kenneth is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad has been discharged from hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The KENNET is a river in southern England, a tributary of the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kennet is an English river, a tributary of the Thames, so a flower here.

clue.text: Utter cry of pain

parts.note: to utter loudly is to yell
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: Let out a scream of agony.
explanation.walkthrough: The YELLOW is China's second-longest river, not the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yellow River in China is one of the world's great rivers.

clue.text: Live-in partner giving me a motor

indicators.note: the letters give, yielding into a new shape

explanation.surface: A lodger hands the speaker a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A roommate is someone who shares your room or home.

clue.text: Ape taking note

parts.note: orang is short for orang-utan, an ape
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A monkey jotting something down.
explanation.walkthrough: The ORANGE is the longest river in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orange River is South Africa's longest river.

clue.text: Howard's name — adapt to last part of a language

parts.note: to fit is to adapt
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

indicators.note: a run of letters is taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Adjusting a family name to fit a final portion of a language.
explanation.walkthrough: The Howards, Dukes of Norfolk, are also Fitzalan-Howards.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitzalan is part of the family name of the Howard Dukes of Norfolk.

clue.text: King's follower following setter

indicators.note: the ape piece comes after the setter piece

parts.note: the setter is 'me'
Kong follows King in the name of the film ape, King Kong

explanation.surface: The king's attendant walks behind the crossword compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: The MEKONG is the great river of South-East Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mekong is South-East Asia's great river.

clue.text: Overflowing when religious boy breaks it

indicators.note: the nun and the boy break into the word it

parts.note: taken as written
a religious, as a noun, is a member of a religious order such as a nun
Dan is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Something spills over when a pious lad smashes it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'religious' looks like an adjective but is a noun for a nun.
explanation.definitionFit: Inundant means flooding or overflowing.
